name: Electoral system
description: How votes translate into outcomes. Required on every contest, because a result cannot be interpreted without it: 40% of the vote wins outright under first-past-the-post, triggers a runoff under a two-round system, and yields a proportion of seats under a party list. This is the field that lets the profile travel - one that assumed a single system would only work in the country it was written in.

hasDefinedTerm.name: First past the post
hasDefinedTerm.description: Single seat, most votes wins, no majority required.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Block vote
hasDefinedTerm.description: Several seats, voters cast as many votes as there are seats, highest totals win.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Two-round
hasDefinedTerm.description: A second round between leading candidates if no one reaches the threshold in the first.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Party-list proportional
hasDefinedTerm.description: Seats allocated to parties in proportion to their vote share.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Single transferable vote
hasDefinedTerm.description: Multi-seat, ranked, with surplus and eliminated votes transferred.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Mixed-member proportional
hasDefinedTerm.description: Constituency seats plus list seats allocated to make the total proportional.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Parallel or mixed
hasDefinedTerm.description: Constituency and list seats allocated independently, without compensation.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Ranked choice (instant runoff)
hasDefinedTerm.description: Single seat, ranked, lowest eliminated and transferred until a majority.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Approval
hasDefinedTerm.description: Voters approve any number of candidates; most approvals wins.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Indirect
hasDefinedTerm.description: Chosen by an electoral college or a sitting body rather than directly by voters.
